<a id="limes.DefaultListLimit"></a><a id="limes.MaxListLimit"></a>

### limes.DefaultListLimit, limes.MaxListLimit

```go
const (
	DefaultListLimit = 50
	MaxListLimit     = 500
)
```

Page sizes of a list: Limit 0 means DefaultListLimit, anything above MaxListLimit is clamped to it, and a negative Limit is the request's error (Validate).

<a id="limes.DefaultHousekeepingLimit"></a>

### limes.DefaultHousekeepingLimit

```go
const DefaultHousekeepingLimit = 1_000
```

DefaultHousekeepingLimit is how many rows one housekeeping batch — Store.Purge, meter.UsageHousekeeping.ReleaseExpired or PurgeOrphans, meter.LedgerHousekeeping.PurgeCharges — handles when the request names no limit.

<sub>[store.go](../../store.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.MaxDelegationDepth"></a>

### limes.MaxDelegationDepth

```go
const MaxDelegationDepth = 64
```

MaxDelegationDepth is the most ancestors a capability may have: how far IsRevoked walks, and how deep Delegate mints.

<sub>[store.go](../../store.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.MinPurgeRetention"></a>

### limes.MinPurgeRetention

```go
const MinPurgeRetention = MaxLeeway + PurgeClockSkew
```

MinPurgeRetention is the shortest retention Purge takes: no verifier accepts a token longer than MaxLeeway past its expiry, by a clock no more than PurgeClockSkew behind the store's, so a capability expired for longer can lose its revocation entry unseen.

<sub>[store.go](../../store.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.PurgeClockSkew"></a>

### limes.PurgeClockSkew

```go
const PurgeClockSkew = time.Minute
```

PurgeClockSkew is how far the clock of the store that purges may run ahead of a verifier's: the store measures expiry by its own clock, the verifier by its own, and a revocation must outlive the token on both.

<sub>[store.go](../../store.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.ErrConflict"></a>

### limes.ErrConflict

```go
var ErrConflict = errors.New("limes: conflict")
```

ErrConflict is the family of a request that is well formed but disagrees with what is already on record: an id taken, a name already given to another cost, a version someone else moved. Nothing was done; the caller reads again and decides. It matches no ErrInvalidRequest — the request would have succeeded against other state — and a caller maps the whole family to its "conflict" (HTTP 409) without listing it.

<sub>[store.go](../../store.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.ErrCursorRepeated"></a>

### limes.ErrCursorRepeated

```go
var ErrCursorRepeated = errors.New("limes: a page returned a cursor already fetched")
```

ErrCursorRepeated is a page that hands back a cursor the walk has already fetched — its own, or one further back. Following it would fetch the same pages forever, so the walk stops there.

<sub>[pages.go](../../pages.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.ErrNotFound"></a>

### limes.ErrNotFound

```go
var ErrNotFound = errors.New("limes: not found")
```

ErrNotFound is the family of every not-found error: Store.GetRecord returns it, and the meter's not-found sentinels (meter.ErrUsageNotFound and the others) match it under errors.Is. It lives in the core package so that any store can satisfy the Store contract using only what this package publishes.

The verifier never returns it: an id not on record is refused as ErrUnrecorded, or taken as not revoked under VerifierConfig.AllowUnrecorded.

<sub>[store.go](../../store.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.AllByPrincipal"></a>

### limes.AllByPrincipal

```go
func AllByPrincipal(ctx context.Context, l CapabilityLister, req ListByPrincipalRequest) iter.Seq2[Capability, error]
```

AllByPrincipal walks ListByPrincipal page by page, from req.Cursor, and yields every capability in its order. req.Limit sets the page size, not how many are yielded.

An error is yielded once, with a zero Capability, and ends the walk; breaking out of the loop fetches no further page. The cursor is the contract for paging across requests — an API handing a page token to its client — and this is for a caller that wants the whole list in one go.

<sub>[pages.go](../../pages.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.AllPages"></a>

### limes.AllPages

```go
func AllPages[T any](
	ctx context.Context,
	cursor string,
	page func(ctx context.Context, cursor string) (Page[T], error),
) iter.Seq2[T, error]
```

AllPages walks a paged list from cursor, fetching each page with page until one returns an empty cursor, and yields every item in its order, for a lister of a package other than this one; AllByPrincipal is one walk.

An error is yielded once, with a zero T, and ends the walk; so does a page handing back a cursor already fetched (ErrCursorRepeated). Breaking out of the loop fetches no further page.

<sub>[pages.go](../../pages.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.As"></a>

### limes.As

```go
func As[T any](s Store) (T, error)
```

As is s as the optional interface T beside Store — limes.As\[limes.RevocationLineageLookup](store) — or ErrInvalidConfig naming T when s is not one. A store, or a decorator over one, that leaves an optional interface out turns its feature off with no error until it is used; As refuses that where it is called, at startup.

<sub>[store_as.go](../../store_as.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.AsAll"></a>

### limes.AsAll

```go
func AsAll(s Store, targets ...any) error
```

AsAll sets each target, a pointer to an optional interface beside Store, to s, or refuses with ErrInvalidConfig naming every one s is not — one call at startup for every interface a consumer uses. Each target it refuses is left as it was, nil for a fresh variable, so its error is always checked. Whether a target is a pointer to an interface is known only when it runs: one that is not is ErrInvalidRequest, and none is set.

<a id="limes.CountRecordsRequest"></a>

### limes.CountRecordsRequest

```go
type CountRecordsRequest struct {
	// TenantID is the tenant whose records are counted; AllTenants counts
	// every tenant's instead. Exactly one of them is required.
	TenantID   uuid.UUID
	AllTenants bool
	// ExpiringWithin is the window ExpiringSoon counts in: an active record
	// expiring within it of now. Zero counts none; negative is refused.
	ExpiringWithin time.Duration
	// ByTenant and ByPrincipalType group the counts by the record's tenant
	// and by its subject's principal type as well.
	ByTenant, ByPrincipalType bool
	// Subject, OnBehalfOf, ClientID, Session and SubjectIssuer count only
	// the records that match each one set, as RevokeMatching selects them,
	// so a count previews a revocation and audits one after. Every one,
	// RunID's too, is taken with AllTenants: a count changes nothing.
	Subject, OnBehalfOf, ClientID, Session, SubjectIssuer string
	// RunID counts only the records of that agent run, as RevokeMatching
	// selects them.
	RunID uuid.UUID
	// Limit is the page size; see PageLimit. Negative is refused.
	Limit int
	// Cursor is the one the previous page returned; empty for the first.
	Cursor string
}
```

CountRecordsRequest asks for one page of record counts.

<sub>[exchange_store.go](../../exchange_store.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.ExchangeStore"></a>

### limes.ExchangeStore

```go
type ExchangeStore interface {
	// ExchangedFor is the capability recorded for key, or ErrNotFound when
	// there is none. It refuses what ExchangeKey.Validate refuses.
	ExchangedFor(ctx context.Context, key ExchangeKey) (uuid.UUID, error)

	// ClaimExchange records req.CapabilityID as the capability issued for
	// req.Key, and returns it with claimed true. When the key holds a
	// capability already it records nothing and returns that one with
	// claimed false, so concurrent claims of one key converge on one id. The
	// capability must be on record in the key's tenant: ErrNotFound for one
	// that is not, or is another tenant's. The record outlives its
	// capability: Purge and an erase remove it only once req.TokenExpiresAt
	// is past their retention, so a token exchanged once is never exchanged
	// afresh while it can still be presented, and its capability purged
	// answers as gone (Issuer.Reissue: ErrNotFound). It refuses what
	// ClaimExchangeRequest.Validate refuses.
	ClaimExchange(ctx context.Context, req ClaimExchangeRequest) (recorded uuid.UUID, claimed bool, err error)
}
```

ExchangeStore records which capability exchanging a subject token issued, so that one subject token yields one capability across every replica. It holds the capability's id and nothing else: no token is stored, and the token is signed again from the record (Issuer.Reissue).

<sub>[store.go](../../store.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.InsertRequest.Validate"></a>

#### limes.InsertRequest.Validate

```go
func (r InsertRequest) Validate() error
```

Validate refuses, as ErrInvalidRequest, a capability with no id — nothing could read it back, and the zero id is what a root's ParentID holds — one with no expiry: no verifier accepts it, Purge never removes it, and a child under it would outlive nothing — and a child naming a Session or a SubjectIssuer, which takes its parent's. Every text it carries, the capability's included, is valid UTF-8 without NUL (docs/compatibility.md): what a store cannot keep as it is is refused, not kept altered.

<sub>[store.go](../../store.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.IssuanceStore"></a>

### limes.IssuanceStore

```go
type IssuanceStore interface {
	// Insert records a capability at issuance. The persisted row holds
	// the full claim set so admin tooling can show a capability without
	// parsing the JWT, and so audit can correlate without
	// keeping every issued token.
	//
	// req.IssuedBy is the principal that ASKED for the capability, which
	// is not its Subject (the principal it authorises) and not its Issuer
	// (the service that minted it). A delegated capability is requested by
	// its parent's holder; a root one by an operator. It is issuance
	// metadata, not a claim, so it travels beside the Capability rather
	// than in it, which would change the token's frozen wire format.
	//
	// An id already on record returns ErrAlreadyExists and changes nothing.
	// It refuses what InsertRequest.Validate refuses, a parent not on
	// record as ErrInvalidRequest, a child expiring after its parent or in
	// another tenant as ErrDelegationTooWide, a child whose budget names
	// another unit than its parent's as ErrUnitCodeMismatch — metering a
	// child spends from every ancestor, so a lineage counts in one unit —
	// and a child that would have more than MaxDelegationDepth ancestors
	// still on record — counted as IsRevoked counts them — as
	// ErrDelegationTooDeep: Purge and the IsRevoked walk rely on a lineage
	// that is whole, no deeper than the walk reaches, expires from the
	// leaves up and stays in one tenant, so a store that scopes rows by
	// tenant sees all of it. A refused record is not written. A store that
	// knows tenants returns ErrUnknownTenant or ErrTenantDeleted for a
	// tenant it cannot mint for. A store beside a meter.TenantUsageEraser
	// refuses a tenant whose usage it erased as ErrTenantErased, until
	// PurgeOrphans forgets the mark. The Issuer answers ErrDelegationTooDeep
	// and ErrTenantErased as ErrDelegationDepthExceeded and ErrTenantGone:
	// no presented capability was revoked.
	Insert(ctx context.Context, req InsertRequest) error

	// IsRevoked reports whether the capability, or any ancestor of it
	// that is still on record, is in the revocation list. Answering for
	// the chain is what makes revoking an orchestrator stop the workers it
	// spawned. Verifiers gate every request on it, so implementations
	// should make the walk a single round trip (a recursive query),
	// bounded at MaxDelegationDepth ancestors: a capability with more
	// still on record returns ErrDelegationTooDeep, never false. An id not
	// on record is not revoked.
	IsRevoked(ctx context.Context, id uuid.UUID) (bool, error)
}
```

IssuanceStore is what an Issuer needs of storage: to record what it mints, and to know whether a parent it delegates from has been revoked.

<a id="limes.ListRecordsRequest"></a>

### limes.ListRecordsRequest

```go
type ListRecordsRequest struct {
	// TenantID is the tenant whose records are listed; AllTenants lists
	// every tenant's instead. Exactly one of the two is required.
	TenantID uuid.UUID
	// AllTenants lists every tenant's records in one id order, as
	// RevokeMatchingRequest.AllTenants revokes across them: a platform
	// operator's index. It needs a scope admitting every tenant's reads
	// (RecordLister).
	AllTenants bool
	// PrincipalType lists the records issued to principals of that type;
	// unspecified, every type's.
	PrincipalType PrincipalType
	// Subject lists the records issued to that subject exactly, and
	// SubjectPrefix those whose subject starts with it, bytewise; at most
	// one of them. Empty, every subject's.
	Subject, SubjectPrefix string
	// OnBehalfOf, ClientID, Session and SubjectIssuer list only the
	// records that match each one set, as RevokeMatching selects them: a
	// listing of what a revocation would revoke, or did.
	OnBehalfOf, ClientID, Session, SubjectIssuer string
	// RunID lists only the records of that agent run, as RevokeMatching
	// selects them.
	RunID uuid.UUID
	// Dispositions lists the records of any of these dispositions; empty,
	// every record.
	Dispositions []RecordDisposition
	// Order is the id order of the pages; the zero value is ascending.
	Order ListOrder
	// Cursor is the one the previous page returned; empty for the first.
	Cursor string
	// Limit is the page size; see PageLimit. Negative is refused.
	Limit int
}
```

ListRecordsRequest asks for one page of a tenant's records, or of every tenant's. Every filter but the tenant is optional, and the ones set must all hold, across tenants as within one.

<sub>[store.go](../../store.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.RecordCensus"></a>

### limes.RecordCensus

```go
type RecordCensus interface {
	// CountRecords returns one page of counts, each one group's: the
	// records of req.TenantID, or of every tenant with req.AllTenants,
	// grouped by tenant and by principal type when req asks, in that order,
	// each ascending. A group with no record has no row, so the census of
	// no record is an empty page.
	CountRecords(ctx context.Context, req CountRecordsRequest) (Page[RecordCount], error)
}
```

RecordCensus counts capability records by what they are now — active, expired or revoked — for a platform operator's report: the records of one tenant or of every tenant, whole or by tenant and by principal type, with how many expire soon. It reads the store a consumer issues into, so a report counts through it rather than through a store's tables, whose columns are the store's own; a view over those tables could freeze its columns, but not take the store's clock or share these rules with every store. It is a type of its own, beside Store: a reporter holds it, an issuer does not. memstore and pgstore each ship one; storetest checks it when its Env sets one. A RecordLister lists the records it counts, each under the disposition it counts it under.

Each record counts under exactly one disposition, by the store's clock, the one expiry and purging are measured by:

  - Revoked: the record, or an ancestor of it still on record, is revoked — what Store.IsRevoked answers, so a child of a revoked parent is revoked here, unlike ListByPrincipalRequest.IncludeRevoked, which reads a record's own entry. Revoked wins over expired.
  - Expired: not revoked, and its ExpiresAt is not after now, or zero (RecordDispositionExpired). A child expires no later than its parent (Store.Insert), so no ancestor need be read for it.
  - Active: neither.

A Biscuit copy's revocation is not a record's and counts nowhere.

<a id="limes.RecordCount"></a>

### limes.RecordCount

```go
type RecordCount struct {
	TenantID      uuid.UUID
	PrincipalType PrincipalType
	// Total is every record of the group: Active, Expired and Revoked
	// together, each record in one of them.
	Total, Active, Expired, Revoked int64
	// Delegated counts the group's records with a parent, whatever their
	// disposition.
	Delegated int64
	// ExpiringSoon counts the active records expiring within the
	// request's ExpiringWithin of now: a part of Active.
	ExpiringSoon int64
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

<sub>[census.go](../../census.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.RecordDisposition"></a>

### limes.RecordDisposition

```go
type RecordDisposition string
```

RecordDisposition is what a record is now: RecordLister's and RecordCensus's three, under which each record falls exactly once.

<sub>[listing.go](../../listing.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.RecordDispositionUnspecified"></a><a id="limes.RecordDispositionActive"></a><a id="limes.RecordDispositionExpired"></a><a id="limes.RecordDispositionRevoked"></a>

#### limes.RecordDispositionUnspecified, limes.RecordDispositionActive, limes.RecordDispositionExpired, limes.RecordDispositionRevoked

```go
const (
	RecordDispositionUnspecified RecordDisposition = ""
	RecordDispositionActive      RecordDisposition = "active"
	RecordDispositionExpired     RecordDisposition = "expired"
	RecordDispositionRevoked     RecordDisposition = "revoked"
)
```

The dispositions. The zero value, RecordDispositionUnspecified, names none.

RecordDispositionExpired takes a record whose ExpiresAt is zero too: no expiry is not "never expires". Store.Insert refuses a capability without one, so such a record was written around it — a pgstore row from before that check, with a NULL expires\_at, or one inserted by hand.

A disposition is the record's, never its Biscuit copies': a capability whose every copy is revoked stays active while the record is not revoked, and its JWT still verifies. Active is no promise that every credential minted from the record works.

<sub>[listing.go](../../listing.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.RecordDisposition.Validate"></a>

#### limes.RecordDisposition.Validate

```go
func (d RecordDisposition) Validate() error
```

Validate refuses a disposition other than the three, as ErrInvalidRequest.

<sub>[listing.go](../../listing.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.RecordLister"></a>

### limes.RecordLister

```go
type RecordLister interface {
	// ListRecords returns one page of req.TenantID's records — or, with
	// req.AllTenants, of every tenant's together — in id order: ascending,
	// or descending with ListOrderDescending: a capability's id is a
	// UUIDv7, so that is newest first. At most Limit of them, and the
	// cursor of the next page, empty on the last. Each record names its
	// tenant, Record.Capability.Subject.TenantID, and its disposition is
	// the one its own tenant's listing gives it. The cursor is the store's
	// own and opaque, and holds the order and the filters it was handed out
	// for: a cursor of the other order, or of another tenant, of every
	// tenant where a tenant's listing is asked for or the other way round,
	// or of another principal type, subject, subject prefix or set of
	// dispositions, is refused with ErrCursorMismatch. A listing of every
	// tenant needs a scope admitting every tenant's reads — in pgstore,
	// WithAllTenantsReadOnly or WithAllTenants — and is refused with
	// ErrScopeMismatch under a narrower one, never narrowed to it.
	ListRecords(ctx context.Context, req ListRecordsRequest) (Page[RecordListing], error)
}
```

RecordLister lists one tenant's capability records a page at a time, or every tenant's, each with its disposition, for an operator's view of them: every record, or those of a principal type, a subject or a subject prefix, and of the dispositions it asks for, oldest or newest first. It is a type of its own beside Store, as RecordCensus is: a reporter holds it, an issuer does not. memstore's and pgstore's Census are each one; storetest checks it when its Env sets one.

A record's disposition is the one RecordCensus counts it under, by the store's clock: revoked — itself or an ancestor still on record, unlike ListByPrincipalRequest.IncludeRevoked — over expired, over active. So, at one instant, the records of each disposition a full listing yields number what CountRecords counts for the tenant. Each page is read on its own, so a walk of many pages is no snapshot: a record can expire, or be revoked, between two of them. A Biscuit copy's revocation changes no record's disposition (RecordDisposition).

<sub>[listing.go](../../listing.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.RecordListing"></a>

### limes.RecordListing

```go
type RecordListing struct {
	Record      Record
	Disposition RecordDisposition
	// StoppedBy is the entry that makes a revoked record revoked: its own,
	// Record.Revocation, or for a record stopped only through an ancestor
	// the entry of the nearest ancestor still on record that has one. Nil
	// unless Disposition is RecordDispositionRevoked.
	StoppedBy *CapabilityRevocation
}
```

RecordListing is one record of a listing: what GetRecord reads back about it — its own revocation entry among it, none when it is stopped only through an ancestor — its disposition now, and what revoked it.

<sub>[listing.go](../../listing.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.RecordListingReader"></a>

### limes.RecordListingReader

```go
type RecordListingReader interface {
	// GetRecordListing reads the record of id with its disposition; one
	// not on record, or not visible to the caller, is ErrNotFound, as
	// GetRecord answers it.
	GetRecordListing(ctx context.Context, id uuid.UUID) (RecordListing, error)
}
```

RecordListingReader reads one record with its disposition, as a listing gives it: what Store.GetRecord reads back, and the disposition by the rules RecordLister and RecordCensus share, by the store's clock. A consumer showing one record asks it rather than working the disposition out from IsRevoked and the expiry, which would be a second rule beside the store's. The disposition is the record's, whatever its Biscuit copies' (RecordDisposition). A type of its own beside RecordLister, as the lister is beside Store: memstore's and pgstore's Census are each one, and storetest checks it when its Env.Lister is one.

<sub>[listing.go](../../listing.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.RecordReader"></a>

### limes.RecordReader

```go
type RecordReader interface {
	// GetRecord reads back everything Insert and Revoke wrote about a
	// capability: the capability, who issued it, and its own revocation
	// entry if it has one. ErrNotFound when there is no record. For audit
	// and admin reads, and for a reporter that needs a capability's
	// ceilings; Verifier never calls it.
	GetRecord(ctx context.Context, id uuid.UUID) (Record, error)
}
```

RecordReader reads one capability's record. Store implements it; a caller that only reads records — StoredMeterSubject — asks for no more.

```go

	RecordLister

}
```

<sub>[listing.go](../../listing.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.Revocation"></a>

### limes.Revocation

```go
type Revocation struct {
	RevokedAt time.Time
	Note      string
	Actor     string
	// Cascaded reports that the entry was written by a cascading revoke —
	// of this capability or of an ancestor.
	Cascaded bool
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Revocation is one entry of the revocation list, as Revoke wrote it.

<sub>[store.go](../../store.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.RevocationStore"></a>

### limes.RevocationStore

```go
type RevocationStore interface {
	// Revoke adds an entry to the revocation list, and says whether the
	// capability had one already. Idempotent: a duplicate revoke writes
	// nothing for the capability, keeps the first entry, and reports it
	// with RevokeResult.AlreadyRevoked. An id not on record — or not
	// visible to the caller — returns ErrNotFound and writes nothing, so a
	// caller is never told "revoked" about a capability nothing stopped.
	// It refuses what RevokeRequest.Validate refuses.
	//
	// Every descendant stops verifying either way, because IsRevoked
	// walks the chain. CascadeChildren=true additionally writes a
	// revocation entry for each descendant, so the audit trail names
	// every capability that was stopped, not only the one an operator
	// picked. A repeated cascading revoke writes the entries a descendant
	// lacks, whatever the capability's own entry says. A capability already
	// stopped through an ancestor, or expired, still gets its entry: the
	// audit names who revoked it and why, and the entry stands if the
	// ancestor's goes with a purge. RevokeResult.PriorDisposition says it
	// stopped nothing new. A store may keep work per descendant beside the
	// entry — pgstore marks each one revoked, holding its row until the
	// revoke commits — so a revoke's cost can grow with the subtree below
	// the capability, flag or not.
	Revoke(ctx context.Context, req RevokeRequest) (RevokeResult, error)
}
```

RevocationStore revokes one capability. Store implements it; a Revoker, which an admin plane revokes through, asks for no more.

<sub>[store.go](../../store.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.RevokeRequest"></a>

### limes.RevokeRequest

```go
type RevokeRequest struct {
	CapabilityID uuid.UUID
	// Note is an operator-supplied label ("compromise", "rotation",
	// "policy-change"). Stored on the revocation row for audit.
	Note string
	// Actor identifies who triggered the revocation (a user UUID or
	// an automation principal). Stored on the row.
	Actor string
	// CascadeChildren records a revocation entry for every descendant as
	// well. Descendants stop verifying regardless; see Store.Revoke.
	CascadeChildren bool
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

RevokeRequest is the input shape for Store.Revoke.

<sub>[store.go](../../store.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.RevokeRequest.Validate"></a>

#### limes.RevokeRequest.Validate

```go
func (r RevokeRequest) Validate() error
```

Validate refuses, as ErrInvalidRequest, a request naming no capability — nothing could be revoked under the zero id, and answering ErrNotFound would hide the caller's bug — and a Note or Actor that is not valid UTF-8 or holds a NUL.

<sub>[store.go](../../store.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.RevokeResult"></a>

### limes.RevokeResult

```go
type RevokeResult struct {
	// AlreadyRevoked reports that the capability had a revocation entry of
	// its own before the call, so the call wrote none for it. A capability
	// stopped only through an ancestor has none: its first revoke writes
	// one.
	AlreadyRevoked bool
	// Revocation is the capability's entry as it stands after the call:
	// the one the call wrote, or the earlier one it kept, as GetRecord
	// reads it back — at the store's precision.
	Revocation Revocation
	// PriorDisposition is the capability's disposition just before the
	// call, by the rules and the clock RecordCensus and RecordListingReader
	// use: revoked — by its own entry or through an ancestor — then
	// expired, then active. Only a revoke of an active capability stopped
	// something new. AlreadyRevoked implies RecordDispositionRevoked. Unspecified when the
	// store could not tell — a chain past MaxDelegationDepth — though it
	// wrote the entry all the same.
	PriorDisposition RecordDisposition
}
```

RevokeResult is what Store.Revoke did to the capability it names.

<sub>[store.go](../../store.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.Store"></a>

### limes.Store

```go
type Store interface {
	IssuanceStore
	RecordReader
	RevocationStore

	// Purge removes the capabilities expired for longer than the request's
	// retention (PurgeRequest.Retention) — their records, their revocation
	// entries and those of their Biscuit copies — at most req.Limit of
	// them, and reports how many records it removed. A housekeeping worker
	// calls it until a batch comes back short of the limit. The retention
	// is how long an expired capability stays on record for audit, and
	// never less than MinPurgeRetention: a verifier still accepts a token
	// for up to its Leeway past expiry, and a revocation purged before
	// that would let a revoked token through again.
	//
	// Purge never removes a capability while a child of it stays on record:
	// a child expires no later than its parent (Insert refuses one that
	// would not), and among records expiring together Purge takes the
	// deepest first. The IsRevoked walk and the meter.Meter's lineage, which
	// stop at the first ancestor no longer on record, therefore miss no
	// revocation and no ceiling. Once records go,
	// meter.UsageHousekeeping.PurgeOrphans releases what the meter still
	// holds for them.
	Purge(ctx context.Context, req PurgeRequest) (PurgeResult, error)

	// ListByPrincipal lists the capabilities issued to one principal, in
	// ascending id order, a page at a time: at most Limit of them, and the
	// cursor of the next page, empty on the last. The cursor is the store's
	// own and opaque.
	ListByPrincipal(ctx context.Context, req ListByPrincipalRequest) (Page[Capability], error)
}
```

Store persists capability records and revocation entries. Consumers supply the implementation: memstore ships an in-memory one, and the module github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes/pgstore one over PostgreSQL.

Records are append-mostly: capabilities aren't mutated after issuance except via Revoke. Revocations are checked by the verifier on every request; put a RevocationCache in front to keep the per-call cost flat.

<sub>[store.go](../../store.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.TenantRecordEraser"></a>

### limes.TenantRecordEraser

```go
type TenantRecordEraser interface {
	// EraseTenantRecords revokes every capability of the tenant not revoked
	// yet, so no token of the tenant verifies again, and removes those of
	// its records Purge would remove at MinPurgeRetention — each with its
	// revocation entry and its Biscuit copies' — and no other: an id not on
	// record is not revoked, so a record removed while its token may still
	// verify would let that token through again. Purge takes the rest as
	// it expires. It changes no other tenant's records, and a second call
	// revokes and removes nothing the first left.
	EraseTenantRecords(ctx context.Context, req EraseTenantRequest) (EraseTenantResult, error)
}
```

TenantRecordEraser is a Store that erases one tenant's capability records, for a consumer removing the tenant. It is optional; storetest checks a Store that implements it.

<sub>[erase_tenant.go](../../erase_tenant.go)</sub>

<a id="memstore"></a><a id="package-memstore"></a>

## Package memstore

`import "github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes/memstore"`

Package memstore is an in-memory reference implementation of the limes storage contracts.

It exists for three reasons, in order of importance:

 1. It proves the contracts are satisfiable without a relational database — the module's own suite runs against it with no database, no network and no container.
 2. It is the worked example a third party reads before writing their own store. Everything here is deliberately obvious rather than fast.
 3. Its Charge carries a staging-commit semantic, which is what makes the atomicity guarantee demonstrable at all. Without one, no implementation in the module could show that a failed side effect leaves counters unmutated.

The record store is also a limes.BiscuitRevocationStore, a limes.BulkRevoker and a limes.ExchangeStore. NewLedger reads a usage store's ledger as a meter.LedgerReader and purges it as a meter.LedgerHousekeeping, NewCensus counts a record store's records as a limes.RecordCensus and lists them as a limes.RecordLister, and the stores erase a tenant as limes.TenantRecordEraser and meter.TenantUsageEraser; EraseTenantUsage leaves a mark on the usage store's Records store, whose Insert then refuses the tenant with limes.ErrTenantErased until PurgeOrphans forgets it.

It is NOT a production store: each store keeps its maps behind one mutex, which the usage store holds while onCharged runs, nothing survives a restart, and the charges ledger grows until Ledger.PurgeCharges removes charges past their retention, or EraseTenantUsage a tenant's.

<a id="memstore.UsageStore.Charge"></a>

#### memstore.UsageStore.Charge

```go
func (s *UsageStore) Charge(
	ctx context.Context,
	req meter.ChargeRequest,
	onCharged func(ctx context.Context, c meter.Charged) error,
) (meter.ChargeReceipt, error)
```

Charge applies the ceiling chain and commits atomically.

The staging semantic is the point of this method: every mutation is computed into locals, onCharged runs, and only if it succeeds are the counters and the ledger published. A rejection by any ceiling, or an error from onCharged, therefore leaves EVERY counter and the ledger exactly as they were — which is the atomicity guarantee.

### memstore.UsageStoreConfig

```go
type UsageStoreConfig struct {
	// Records is how the usage store finds each capability's ancestors and
	// their ceilings, and which capabilities still exist for PurgeOrphans.
	// Required: without it no ancestor's ceiling would bind, which a store
	// over a database never does. It is the Store that serves Insert: the
	// mark EraseTenantUsage leaves, which makes Insert refuse the tenant, is
	// kept there.
	Records *Store
	// Now is the clock, read as a wall clock (wallClock). Nil: time.Now.
	Now func() time.Time
	// MaxCopiesPerCapability is how many Biscuit copies the store counts
	// for one capability (meter.Meter, "Copies of a Biscuit"). Zero:
	// meter.DefaultMaxCopiesPerCapability; negative is refused.
	MaxCopiesPerCapability int
}
```

<a id="pgstore"></a><a id="package-pgstore"></a>

## Package pgstore

`import "github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes/pgstore"`

Package pgstore is the reference implementation of the limes storage contracts over PostgreSQL: limes.Store, limes.BiscuitRevocationStore, limes.RevocationLineageLookup and limes.BulkRevoker for capability records and revocations, limes.ExchangeStore for token exchange, meter.UsageStore, meter.CopyUsageReader, meter.Leaser, meter.MatchingReleaser and meter.TenantReservationLister for the meter, meter.LedgerReader, limes.RecordCensus, limes.RecordLister and limes.RecordListingReader for reports, meter.LedgerHousekeeping for bounding the ledger, limes.TenantRecordEraser and meter.TenantUsageEraser for removing a tenant, and dpop.ReplayCache (ReplayCache) for DPoP proof ids shared by every replica of a verifier. It passes the module's own contract suites, storetest and metertest, which is how a consumer knows it keeps every rule a store must keep.

Create the schema once, as the role that owns it, with pgstore/migrate — which a migration job alone imports, so a binary that serves links none of it — granting the role the stores serve as; then build both stores over a pool of that role:

	err := ownerPool.AcquireFunc(ctx, func(c *pgxpool.Conn) error {
		return migrate.Run(ctx, c.Conn(), migrate.Options{RuntimeRoles: []string{"app"}})
	})
	records, err := pgstore.NewStore(pgstore.Config{DB: pool})
	usage, err := pgstore.NewUsageStore(pgstore.Config{DB: pool})

CheckSchema returns ErrSchemaMismatch while the schema is not the version this package queries, and ErrRuntimeRole when the pool is a role the policies do not hold — a superuser, one with BYPASSRLS, an owner of the schema or of anything in it, or a role that can act as one — asked of the current role, the session's and the one the connection logged in as, since a session opened as such a role can reset back to it — for a readiness check; ReadSchemaVersion reports both versions and needs only the SELECT that migrate.Run grants a runtime role.

The schema needs PostgreSQL 15 or later: the meter reads the records through a view that runs as its caller (security\_invoker), so their row-level security binds it as it binds a read of the table.

Every call runs in READ COMMITTED transactions on one connection, whatever the database's default — one per call, but for a call that settles leases, each in a transaction of its own, and for the revocation checks (IsRevoked, IsBiscuitRevoked, RevocationLineage), each a single statement (see Tenants) — and every time it writes or compares against comes from Config.Now, but one: with Config.Now nil, the usage store measures holds' and leases' expiry by the database's clock, now(), the time its transaction began. The replicas of a service share the database and not their clocks: one running ahead would release another's live holds as expired, or refuse their Settle with meter.ErrReservationNotFound. One clock writes and compares a hold's lifetime — its expiry is the database's time plus its TTL, and Settle, Reserve, Lease, a charge or a bump under a lease and ReleaseExpired decide by it. With Config.Now set, that clock decides expiry too, as a test that moves it needs.

A capability's expiry is another clock's: the issuer's, which wrote it, and whether the token has expired is its verifier's to decide, by its own clock and leeway. The store does not decide it again by its clock. It ends a hold or a lease no later than the capability's expiry plus a grace — limes.MaxLeeway, the widest leeway a verifier gives, and limes.PurgeClockSkew, how far behind the store's its clock may run — and refuses Reserve and Lease with limes.ErrExpired only past that, where no verifier could still accept the token and its record may be purged (limes.MinPurgeRetention).

Charge and Settle hand onCharged the charge's transaction, and Refund hands onRefunded the refund's, which TxFrom reads from its context, so a write of the consumer's commits with the charge or the refund or not at all. The transaction is the store's to end: Commit and Rollback on it return ErrChargeTransaction, a call whose transaction the callback ended with SQL of its own is refused with ErrChargeTransaction, and once the callback returns every call on it fails with pgx.ErrTxClosed.

#### Tenants

Every table keeps its rows' tenant, and the schema's row-level security binds every role — the tables' owner too — to the tenant a call is scoped to, short of a superuser or a role with BYPASSRLS: pass WithTenant(ctx, tenant) to a call for one tenant, WithAllTenants(ctx) to housekeeping (Purge, ReleaseExpired, PurgeOrphans, Ledger.PurgeCharges), and WithAllTenantsReadOnly(ctx) to a read across tenants, such as ListTenantBudgets: its policies admit reads only, and a call that writes under it is refused with limes.ErrScopeMismatch, as one is under a Scope of the consumer's that sets the same read-only setting. A call scoped to none sees no row and writes none. IsRevoked and IsBiscuitRevoked see every tenant whatever the scope: the verifier asks them before it knows the token's tenant, on every request, so each is one statement calling a function of the schema that runs as the tables' owner and scopes itself to every tenant, read only, for its own query — one round trip, no transaction. Only the roles migrate.Run grants (migrate.Options.RuntimeRoles) may execute the schema's functions. migrate.Run runs as the owner, scoped to every tenant for its run; serve as a role that owns nothing, which CheckSchema checks, so that no call can turn the policies off. Config.CheckTenant lets a consumer that keeps its own tenants refuse one it does not hold.

A call whose request names its tenant — Insert, ListByPrincipal, RevokeMatching, ExchangedFor, ClaimExchange, Bump, Charge, Reserve, Settle, Release, Lease, SettleLease, ListTenantReservations, GetTenantBudget, SetTenantBudget, the erasers, and ReleaseMatching, Ledger.SumCharges, Census.ListRecords and Census.CountRecords for one tenant — under a scope that does not admit that tenant returns limes.ErrScopeMismatch rather than answer as if the tenant's rows were not there (Config.CheckScope). A call that names only an id cannot be checked so, and answers a row out of scope as not found.

The schema notifies RevocationChannel on every statement that writes a revocation; a RevocationWatcher beside each verifier clears its revocation caches then, so a revocation reaches every replica at once rather than within the caches' TTL.

A Ledger sums a tenant's charges for billing and reports (meter.LedgerReader), and removes those past their retention (meter.LedgerHousekeeping), so a consumer reads the ledger through it rather than through the charges table, whose columns are this package's own. A Census counts the capability records (limes.RecordCensus) for the same reason: of one tenant, scoped to it as every call naming a tenant, or of every tenant under WithAllTenantsReadOnly or WithAllTenants — a scope that admits fewer is refused with limes.ErrScopeMismatch, not counted as all. It lists a tenant's records too (limes.RecordLister), and reads one (limes.RecordListingReader), each with the disposition it counts them under, scoped to that tenant.

To remove a tenant, Store.EraseTenant revokes its capabilities, removes the records Purge would and every meter row of the tenant — the charges ledger included — in one transaction, and runs the consumer's own removal in it. It marks the tenant erased, as EraseTenantUsage does, so Insert and the meter refuse it with limes.ErrTenantErased afterwards; PurgeOrphans forgets the mark once none of the tenant's records is left. The records it keeps stay revoked until Purge takes them: an id not on record is not revoked, so a token whose record went early would verify again. TenantTables lists the tables that hold a tenant's rows, and what the erase does to each.

#### Throughput

A tenant's ceiling holds exactly because every call that moves the tenant's spend or holds — Charge, Reserve, Settle, Refund, Release, ReleaseExpired, Lease, SettleLease, SetTenantBudget — locks the tenant's budget row for the rest of its transaction. One tenant's charges therefore commit one at a time, whichever capabilities they are on: its throughput is about one charge per charge transaction, and adding connections or replicas does not raise it. Different tenants' charges do not wait on each other, nor does any tenant's Bump, which counts requests and takes no tenant lock, nor IsRevoked. In the package's benchmarks, against PostgreSQL on the same host, a charge transaction took 1.4–3ms — some 350–700 charges a second for one tenant (BenchmarkChargeParallel beside BenchmarkChargeParallelTenants). A network between the service and the database adds its round trip to every statement of the transaction, and onCharged and onRefunded run inside it, holding the lock: keep them short. A tenant that needs more charges a second than that is a sizing question — fewer, larger charges, as Reserve and Settle allow, or a lease for each worker, whose charges lock the lease and not the row — not a setting. A tenant with no ceiling counted in stripes locks no row at all: its calls add to a stripe of their connection's (docs/adr/0022-unlimited-tenant-aggregate.md).

<a id="pgstore.SettingTenant"></a><a id="pgstore.SettingAllTenants"></a><a id="pgstore.SettingAllTenantsOn"></a><a id="pgstore.SettingAllTenantsRead"></a>

### pgstore.SettingTenant, pgstore.SettingAllTenants, pgstore.SettingAllTenantsOn, pgstore.SettingAllTenantsRead

```go
const (
	// SettingTenant holds the tenant a transaction is scoped to, as a
	// UUID's text.
	SettingTenant = "limes.tenant_id"
	// SettingAllTenants is SettingAllTenantsOn in a transaction scoped to
	// every tenant, and SettingAllTenantsRead in one that may read every
	// tenant's rows and write none.
	SettingAllTenants     = pgschema.SettingAllTenants
	SettingAllTenantsOn   = pgschema.SettingAllTenantsOn
	SettingAllTenantsRead = "read"
)
```

The settings the row-level security policies read (migrate/ddl/migrations/ 003\_row\_security.sql), each set local to one transaction. A Scope of the consumer's (Config.Scope) that sets them is scoped as the package's own is, and CheckSchemaScope reads them back.

<a id="pgstore.MaxNotifiedRevocations"></a><a id="pgstore.MaxNotifiedRevocationsPerStatement"></a>

### pgstore.MaxNotifiedRevocations, pgstore.MaxNotifiedRevocationsPerStatement

```go
const (
	// MaxNotifiedRevocations is the most capability ids one notification
	// names: a hundred ids are some 3.7 KB of a payload PostgreSQL bounds
	// at 8000 bytes.
	MaxNotifiedRevocations = 100
	// MaxNotifiedRevocationsPerStatement is the most capability ids one
	// statement's notifications name, MaxNotifiedRevocations at a time:
	// past it, one notification names none, and a cache is cleared whole.
	// It is limes.DefaultHousekeepingLimit, so a batch of RevokeMatching at
	// its default limit drops only what it outdates.
	MaxNotifiedRevocationsPerStatement = limes.DefaultHousekeepingLimit
)
```

The bounds of the ids a statement's revocations are notified with (migrate/ddl/migrations/028\_notify\_revocations\_in\_parts.sql spells both too, and a test holds the two to one number each).

<a id="pgstore.ErrRuntimeRole"></a>

### pgstore.ErrRuntimeRole

```go
var ErrRuntimeRole = fmt.Errorf("%w: pgstore: the store is served by a role row-level security does not hold", limes.ErrInvalidConfig)
```

ErrRuntimeRole is CheckSchema finding the store served by a role row-level security does not hold to its tenant: a superuser or a role with BYPASSRLS, which it never binds, or an owner of the schema or of anything in it, which may turn it off or replace what enforces it — that role itself, or one it can act as (SET ROLE) or inherits from. The owner migrates; a role that owns nothing serves (migrate.Options.RuntimeRoles).

<a id="pgstore.CheckSchema"></a>

### pgstore.CheckSchema

```go
func CheckSchema(ctx context.Context, db DB) error
```

CheckSchema is a readiness check for the stores over db. It returns ErrSchemaMismatch when the schema is not at the version this package queries — a store over it would fail on a table or column it expects — and ErrRuntimeRole when db is served by a role row-level security does not hold to its tenant, so a store over it would isolate no tenant.

### pgstore.CheckSchemaScope

```go
func CheckSchemaScope(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, tenant uuid.UUID) error
```

CheckSchemaScope refuses with limes.ErrScopeMismatch a transaction whose scope, as the schema's settings hold it, does not admit tenant — scoped to another tenant, or to none — when row-level security binds its role. It is a Config.CheckScope for a Scope of the consumer's that sets those settings.

<a id="pgstore.ScopeFromContext"></a>

### pgstore.ScopeFromContext

```go
func ScopeFromContext(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx) error
```

ScopeFromContext is the Scope a store uses when Config sets none: it sets the settings the schema's policies read from WithTenant, WithAllTenants or WithAllTenantsReadOnly. It sets both of them every time — the one the scope does not use to nothing — so a default the role, the database or the session gives either one cannot widen the scope: a call scoped to no tenant sees no row, whatever the defaults.

<a id="pgstore.ScopedIssuance"></a>

### pgstore.ScopedIssuance

```go
func ScopedIssuance(s *Store) limes.IssuanceStore
```

ScopedIssuance is s as the limes.IssuanceStore of an Issuer that issues where no tenant is in scope — behind a token endpoint, whose requests name none: Insert runs scoped to the tenant of the capability it records, as WithTenant scopes it, so row-level security admits the record whatever the caller's context says. IsRevoked sees every tenant already, and GetRecord reads every tenant's, read-only, for Issuer.Reissue. It scopes through the context, so a Config.Scope of the consumer's that does not read WithTenant gains nothing from it.

<sub>[pgstore/issuance.go](../../pgstore/issuance.go)</sub>
<a id="pgstore.TxFrom"></a>

### pgstore.TxFrom

```go
func TxFrom(ctx context.Context) (pgx.Tx, bool)
```

TxFrom returns the transaction a charge or a refund commits on, from the context UsageStore.Charge and UsageStore.Settle hand onCharged, and UsageStore.Refund onRefunded: a write through it commits with the charge or the refund, or with it not at all. Any other context holds none, and TxFrom reports false; no other method of this package reads a transaction from its context.

The call's writes are in it already — a charge's ledger row, a refund's refunded amount on the charge and, under a RefundID, its limes.refunds row — and its locks held: every counter on the chain and the tenant's aggregate, which every other charge of the tenant waits for until the callback returns and the store commits. The callback keeps to statements on this database, and short ones; a network call there holds the tenant's charges for as long.

The transaction is the callback's while it runs, and no longer: once it returns, every call on it, from any goroutine, fails with pgx.ErrTxClosed, and a call still running then is waited for before the store commits. Calls are taken one at a time, as a pgx.Tx needs. Commit and Rollback return ErrChargeTransaction; a savepoint (Begin) is the callback's to end. Conn is nil, as the connection is the store's, and a call whose transaction the callback ended with SQL of its own — COMMIT, ROLLBACK, or either followed by BEGIN — is refused with ErrChargeTransaction and meter.ErrOutcomeUnknown: the call's writes went before the callback, so that COMMIT committed them, and that ROLLBACK undid them.

<sub>[pgstore/tx.go](../../pgstore/tx.go)</sub>
<a id="pgstore.WithAllTenants"></a>

### pgstore.WithAllTenants

```go
func WithAllTenants(ctx context.Context) context.Context
```

WithAllTenants scopes the calls made with ctx to every tenant, to read and write: for housekeeping (Store.Purge, UsageStore.ReleaseExpired and PurgeOrphans, Ledger.PurgeCharges) and for RevokeMatching and ReleaseMatching with AllTenants. A read across tenants takes WithAllTenantsReadOnly. A call scoped to none sees no row at all.

<sub>[pgstore/scope.go](../../pgstore/scope.go)</sub>
<a id="pgstore.WithAllTenantsReadOnly"></a>

### pgstore.WithAllTenantsReadOnly

```go
func WithAllTenantsReadOnly(ctx context.Context) context.Context
```

WithAllTenantsReadOnly scopes the calls made with ctx to reading every tenant's rows — ListTenantBudgets, a dashboard, an admin lookup — and writing none: the schema's policies admit no write under it, and a call that writes is refused with limes.ErrScopeMismatch before it begins. A Scope of the consumer's gets the same refusal by setting limes.all\_tenants to 'read' (Config.Scope).

<a id="pgstore.Config"></a>

### pgstore.Config

```go
type Config struct {
	// DB is the database, its schema created by migrate.Run. Required: nil, or a
	// nil pool or connection, is refused at construction.
	DB DB
	// Now is the store's clock. Nil: time.Now, and the database's clock,
	// now(), for holds' and leases' expiry (see the package documentation).
	// A capability's expiry is its verifier's to decide by its own clock:
	// the store refuses one only past the grace a verifier's leeway takes.
	Now func() time.Time
	// Scope runs first in every transaction the store opens, with the call's
	// context, and sets what row-level security policies read: nil is
	// ScopeFromContext, which serves the schema's own policies from
	// WithTenant, WithAllTenants and WithAllTenantsReadOnly. A consumer with policies of its own sets
	// its settings here (set_config(…, true), local to the transaction). An
	// error from it ends the call.
	//
	// What it sends with tx.Exec goes with the call's first statement, in
	// one batch, so it costs no round trip of its own: such an Exec returns
	// an empty command tag and no error at once, and a statement of it that
	// fails fails that first statement as the scope's error. A query it
	// sends with Query or QueryRow is sent as before, what it executed
	// first going with it.
	//
	// A Scope of the consumer's that scopes a call to reading every tenant
	// sets limes.all_tenants to 'read', as WithAllTenantsReadOnly does: a
	// call that writes then reads the setting back once Scope has run, and
	// refuses with limes.ErrScopeMismatch before it writes anything —
	// whatever limes.tenant_id says beside it, and one round trip more per
	// call that writes. A Scope that never sets limes.all_tenants to 'read'
	// gets no such check; its policies alone decide what a write reaches.
	Scope func(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx) error
	// CheckTenant, when set, runs in Insert's transaction before the record
	// is written, for a consumer that keeps its own tenants: it returns
	// limes.ErrUnknownTenant for a tenant it does not hold and
	// limes.ErrTenantDeleted for one in the trash, which Insert returns
	// as they are. Nil: every tenant is one the store can mint for.
	CheckTenant func(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, tenant uuid.UUID) error
	// CheckScope runs after Scope in the transaction of every call whose
	// request names its tenant — Insert, ListByPrincipal, RevokeMatching,
	// ExchangedFor, ClaimExchange, Bump, Charge, Reserve, Settle, Release,
	// Lease, SettleLease, ListTenantReservations, GetTenantBudget,
	// SetTenantBudget, EraseTenant, EraseTenantRecords, EraseTenantUsage, and
	// ReleaseMatching, Ledger.SumCharges, Census.ListRecords and
	// Census.CountRecords for one tenant — and refuses one whose scope does not admit that tenant with limes.ErrScopeMismatch,
	// which the call returns as it is. Nil, under the default Scope: the
	// call's WithTenant or WithAllTenants decides, and with neither
	// CheckSchemaScope does. Nil beside a Scope of the consumer's: no check,
	// since the store cannot tell what its policies admit; a Scope that sets
	// the schema's own settings passes CheckSchemaScope here.
	CheckScope func(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, tenant uuid.UUID) error
	// Logger logs what a store does that its caller does not see: a meter
	// call retried after PostgreSQL aborted it to break a deadlock. Nil:
	// slog.Default().
	Logger *slog.Logger
	// Events are the callbacks the usage store makes as it works
	// (meter.StoreEvents): how long each metered call waited for its
	// tenant's aggregate, among them. Each is optional; the zero value
	// makes none. otelmetric.NewStoreEvents records them as metrics. The
	// record store ignores it.
	Events meter.StoreEvents
	// DisableLeases stops the usage store opening leases
	// (meter.Leaser.Lease): Lease refuses with meter.ErrLeasingDisabled,
	// while leases already open are still charged under and settled. Unset,
	// a lease is opened only when Lease asks for one; a store that opens
	// none pays one statement per charge and bump a lease could cover, a
	// read of the chain's leases in the batch the call sends already, set
	// or not. A release before pgstore/v0.58.0 reads none of a lease's
	// state, so set it while one still writes the database, and before
	// going back to one, then settle every lease (docs/migration.md).
	DisableLeases bool
	// MaxCopiesPerCapability is how many Biscuit copies the usage store
	// counts for one capability (meter.Meter, "Copies of a Biscuit"). Zero:
	// meter.DefaultMaxCopiesPerCapability; negative is refused. The record
	// store ignores it.
	MaxCopiesPerCapability int
	// DisableTenantStripes has the usage store count a tenant with no
	// ceiling on its aggregate's one row, every call locking it. Unset,
	// such a tenant is counted in stripes
	// (docs/adr/0022-unlimited-tenant-aggregate.md): its calls read the row
	// without locking it and add their change to the stripe of their
	// connection, so they do not queue on one row. A store folds the
	// stripes into the row, and sums them when it reads the aggregate,
	// whether it is set or not. A release before pgstore/v0.72.0 reads the
	// row without its stripes, and checks a ceiling set meanwhile against
	// less than was spent: set it while one still writes the database
	// (docs/migration.md). The record store ignores it.
	DisableTenantStripes bool
	// TenantBudgetLockTimeout is how long SetTenantBudget waits for the
	// tenant's calls in flight before it changes nothing and refuses with a
	// meter.TenantBudgetBusyError
	// (docs/adr/0022-unlimited-tenant-aggregate.md, Decision 9). Every call
	// of the tenant that starts meanwhile queues behind it, so it is also
	// the longest the tenant is stalled. Zero: 5s. Below a millisecond,
	// which PostgreSQL's lock_timeout cannot express, is refused, as is
	// negative. The record store ignores it.
	TenantBudgetLockTimeout time.Duration
}
```

Config configures a store.

<sub>[pgstore/pgstore.go](../../pgstore/pgstore.go)</sub>
<a id="pgstore.ConnLender"></a>

### pgstore.ConnLender

```go
type ConnLender interface {
	LendConn(ctx context.Context) (*pgxpool.Conn, error)
}
```

ConnLender is a DB of your own that lends a connection from a pool for one call, opting in to sending BEGIN and COMMIT in the call's batches (DB). A Config.DB that implements it, found there by type assertion, has each call take a connection with LendConn, send its statements on it, and release it once the transaction has ended: rolled back first when it failed, so it goes back to the pool outside a transaction. Its BeginTx then serves no call that LendConn served: a wrapper that sets session state or traces in BeginTx does it on the lent connection instead, or does not implement ConnLender. No pgx type has the method, so a type that embeds a \*pgxpool.Pool does not implement it by accident.

<sub>[pgstore/pgstore.go](../../pgstore/pgstore.go)</sub>
<a id="pgstore.DB"></a>

### pgstore.DB

```go
type DB interface {
	BeginTx(ctx context.Context, opts pgx.TxOptions) (pgx.Tx, error)
	QueryRow(ctx context.Context, sql string, args ...any) pgx.Row
}
```

DB is what the store needs of a connection pool: a transaction per call, and a single statement for a revocation check. \*pgxpool.Pool and \*pgx.Conn implement it. A DB of your own opens each transaction with the options it is given: one that drops them leaves the store at the database's default isolation, which txOptions exists to override. It stays these two methods for all of v1.

A DB that is a \*pgxpool.Pool or a \*pgx.Conn, or implements ConnLender — each found by type assertion — runs each call on a connection of its own and sends BEGIN with the call's first statement, and a meter call's COMMIT with its last batch: no round trip of their own (docs/adr/0018-fewer-round-trips-per-charge.md). Its BeginTx then serves no call. Any other DB has each transaction opened by BeginTx and committed by the transaction's Commit, a round trip each: a type of your own that embeds a \*pgxpool.Pool among them, so a BeginTx it overrides is always called.

<sub>[pgstore/pgstore.go](../../pgstore/pgstore.go)</sub>

<a id="pgstore.Ledger"></a>

### pgstore.Ledger

```go
type Ledger struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Ledger implements meter.LedgerReader and meter.LedgerHousekeeping over the store's charges ledger.

A charge carries the store's time, so a test of a report backdates its charges through Config.Now rather than by writing the charges table, whose columns are this package's own: build the stores on a clock the test sets, record a capability that outlives the period, and move the clock forward before each charge.

	at := start
	cfg := pgstore.Config{DB: pool, Now: func() time.Time { return at }}
	records, _ := pgstore.NewStore(cfg)
	usage, _ := pgstore.NewUsageStore(cfg)
	_ = records.Insert(ctx, limes.InsertRequest{Capability: c}) // c.ExpiresAt past the period
	subject, _ := limes.StoredMeterSubject(ctx, records, c.ID)
	at = start.AddDate(0, 0, 1)
	_, _ = usage.Charge(ctx, meter.ChargeRequest{Subject: subject, Amount: amount}, nil)

<a id="pgstore.ReplayCache"></a>

### pgstore.ReplayCache

```go
type ReplayCache struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

ReplayCache is a dpop.ReplayCache over PostgreSQL: one table, limes.dpop\_seen\_proofs, that every replica of a verifier shares, so a proof accepted on one is refused on all of them until it expires.

It is for a deployment that runs pgstore already and would rather not run Redis (redisreplay) beside it, or keep the ids in one process alone (dpop.MemoryReplayCache). The check runs as the runtime role before any tenant is known: the table has no row-level security, and the cache sets no scope.

Each holder — the capability whose proofs they are — has a share of the cache: Seen refuses, with dpop.ErrReplayQuota, an id of a holder that already has EntriesPerHolder live ids, whatever key signed them. The count and the insert happen under a transaction-scoped advisory lock on the holder, so concurrent proofs of one holder never take it past its share. Such a refusal, unlike a replay, is logged at WARN. The share caps a holder's rate: an id is kept for the verifier's window plus dpop.ReplayClockSkew, so one holder passes at most EntriesPerHolder proofs over that span — with the defaults 1,000 per 65 s, about 15 a second.

What is live is decided by Now, the verifier's clock, never the database's. An expired id counts for nothing, and the same id may take its place; PurgeExpired deletes expired ids, which a job should call until it returns 0.

<a id="pgstore.RevocationWatcher"></a>

### pgstore.RevocationWatcher

```go
type RevocationWatcher struct {
	// Connect opens the connection the watcher listens on. It must be the
	// watcher's own, not one a pool takes back with the LISTEN still on
	// it: from a pool, Acquire and Hijack. Required.
	Connect func(ctx context.Context) (*pgx.Conn, error)
	// Caches are the caches cleared.
	Caches []Clearer
	// OnError, when set, hears each failure the watcher recovers from by
	// connecting again.
	OnError func(error)
	// Heartbeat is how long the watcher waits for a notification before it
	// pings the connection, with as long again for the answer: a ping that
	// fails or does not come back ends the connection as a lost one does,
	// and a signalled cache is told NotListening. A connection that died without a
	// word — a host gone, a network cut — would otherwise go on vouching
	// for the caches until TCP gave up on it, minutes later, while they
	// serve their SyncedTTL; with it, for at most twice Heartbeat. Zero:
	// DefaultWatchHeartbeat. Negative is refused.
	Heartbeat time.Duration
}
```

RevocationWatcher clears revocation caches when any replica revokes: it listens on RevocationChannel and, on each notification, drops from each cache what the revocation outdates — with ClearRevoked, from a RevokedClearer, when the notification names the capabilities revoked — or clears it whole: a cache that is no RevokedClearer, a notification that names none (a Biscuit copy's revocation, a statement revoking more than MaxNotifiedRevocationsPerStatement capabilities that no ancestor's id covers), and after each connection it opens, since a revocation made while it was not listening sent a notification it never heard. A cache that is a limes.RevocationSignalTarget is told instead, through a limes.RevocationSignal Run opens on it and closes when it returns — Listening once it listens, Revoked or RevokedAll on each notification, Renew on each notification and each heartbeat answered, and NotListening when the connection is lost — so it serves its TTL alone while no notification can reach it, and when the watcher stops renewing without a word. Between connections, that TTL bounds how long a revocation may go unseen.

Connect reaches the primary: PostgreSQL notifies only the sessions of the server a revocation committed on, and a hot standby refuses LISTEN, so a watcher pointed at one never listens and its caches stay on their TTL.


<a id="pgstore.Store.EraseTenantRecords"></a>

#### pgstore.Store.EraseTenantRecords

```go
func (s *Store) EraseTenantRecords(ctx context.Context, req limes.EraseTenantRequest) (limes.EraseTenantResult, error)
```

EraseTenantRecords implements limes.TenantRecordEraser: it revokes every capability of the tenant not revoked yet and removes the records Purge would remove at limes.MinPurgeRetention, in one transaction scoped to the tenant (Config.CheckScope).

<a id="pgstore.Store.Insert"></a>

#### pgstore.Store.Insert

```go
func (s *Store) Insert(ctx context.Context, req limes.InsertRequest) error
```

Insert records req.Capability and who asked for it. The parent must be on record (else limes.ErrInvalidRequest), in the same tenant and expire no earlier than the child (else limes.ErrDelegationTooWide), and count its budget in the same unit (else limes.ErrUnitCodeMismatch); the child may have no more than limes.MaxDelegationDepth ancestors on record (else limes.ErrDelegationTooDeep). An id on record is limes.ErrAlreadyExists. A tenant erased by EraseTenant or UsageStore.EraseTenantUsage is refused with limes.ErrTenantErased.

#### pgstore.Store.Purge

```go
func (s *Store) Purge(ctx context.Context, req limes.PurgeRequest) (limes.PurgeResult, error)
```

Purge removes the capabilities expired for longer than the retention, a batch of at most req.Limit (zero: limes.DefaultHousekeepingLimit), and every exchange whose subject token did: an exchange outlives its capability while its token can be presented (limes.ExchangeStore). A scope that admits no tenant is refused with limes.ErrScopeMismatch, rather than purging nothing on every call while the records grow.

<sub>[pgstore/store.go](../../pgstore/store.go)</sub>
<a id="pgstore.Store.RevocationLineage"></a>

#### pgstore.Store.RevocationLineage

```go
func (s *Store) RevocationLineage(ctx context.Context, id uuid.UUID) (limes.RevocationAnswer, error)
```

RevocationLineage implements limes.RevocationLineageLookup: IsRevoked's answer, in one statement as IsRevoked's, and the ancestors on record it read, nearest first; an id not on record is ErrNotFound. Like IsRevoked it reads every tenant whatever the call's scope, so it names the ancestors' ids, and whether an id is on record at all, to the role that calls it: expose it to no one who may not learn another tenant's ids. Migration 020 dropped and recreated limes.revocation\_lineage, and migrate.Run grants it only to migrate.Options.RuntimeRoles: an EXECUTE granted by hand to another role before then is gone and must be granted again.

<sub>[pgstore/store.go](../../pgstore/store.go)</sub>
<a id="pgstore.Store.Revoke"></a>

#### pgstore.Store.Revoke

```go
func (s *Store) Revoke(ctx context.Context, req limes.RevokeRequest) (limes.RevokeResult, error)
```

Revoke writes the capability's revocation entry, and with CascadeChildren one for every descendant. Each entry also marks its record, and every record below it not marked already, revoked — the flag the census and the listing read (migrate/ddl/migrations/015\_revoked\_flag.sql, walked once per statement since 043\_mark\_revoked\_per\_statement.sql) — one UPDATE a generation, by key, inside this transaction. It first takes the tenant's revoke lock alone, which every insert of a child shares (lockForRevoke): the revoke waits for the inserts and revokes of the tenant already running, and those that come after wait for it, so no stream of delegations under the capability holds it back. Its row locks on the subtree then last until it commits. A metered call's lineage lock (FOR KEY SHARE) does not conflict with the mark, so charges neither wait for a revoke nor hold one back. A cascading revoke marks the subtree once, with its root's entry; a capability under one revoked before costs nothing past its own row. The first entry of each stands, and the result carries the capability's.

<sub>[pgstore/store.go](../../pgstore/store.go)</sub>

#### pgstore.Store.RevokeBiscuit

```go
func (s *Store) RevokeBiscuit(ctx context.Context, req limes.RevokeBiscuitRequest) (limes.RevokeBiscuitResult, error)
```

RevokeBiscuit lists one copy's revocation id under its capability; the first entry stands, and the result carries it. The entry another revoke wrote is read in a statement of its own, as Revoke reads one: under READ COMMITTED it sees what committed while the insert waited.

<a id="pgstore.UsageStore"></a>

### pgstore.UsageStore

```go
type UsageStore struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

UsageStore implements meter.UsageStore, meter.CopyUsageReader, meter.Leaser, meter.MatchingReleaser, meter.TenantReservationLister, meter.TenantUsageEraser and meter.FeatureGate: request and spend counters, holds, the charges ledger and the tenant aggregates. It reads each capability's lineage and ceilings from the records a Store over the same database keeps.

Every call locks what it changes in one order — holds by id, then the capabilities' counters by id, then the copies' by revocation id, then the tenant aggregate, then the ledger — so two calls never wait on each other in a cycle (lock\_order\_test.go; docs/adr/0018-fewer-round-trips-per-charge.md). onCharged runs on the call's own transaction, which TxFrom reads from the context it is handed.

A call whose COMMIT left and whose answer did not come back — the connection failed or the context ended first — returns an error matching meter.ErrOutcomeUnknown, wrapping the cause: it may have committed. Bump, Charge, Reserve, Settle, Release, Refund and the leases' calls log it at WARN. One the database answered, or that sent nothing, never does. A keyed id (ChargeRequest.ExternalRef, ReserveRequest.ReservationID, RefundRequest.RefundID) makes the call safe to send again; refunds recorded under one are kept in limes.refunds, removed with their charge.

<a id="migrate"></a><a id="package-migrate"></a>

## Package migrate

`import "github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes/pgstore/migrate"`

Package migrate creates and upgrades the schema pgstore's stores query. Only a migration job imports it: it carries the migrations and runs them with github.com/jackc/tern, which a binary that only serves never links.

Run migrates a database itself. A consumer with a migration tool of its own applies Steps and Grants with that tool instead, from pgstore/migrate/ddl, which holds them without tern.

<a id="migrate.ErrSchemaOwner"></a>

### migrate.ErrSchemaOwner

```go
var ErrSchemaOwner = fmt.Errorf("%w: migrate: the schema belongs to another role", limes.ErrInvalidConfig)
```

ErrSchemaOwner is Run finding the store's schema owned by another role than the one it runs as.

<sub>[pgstore/migrate/migrate.go](../../pgstore/migrate/migrate.go)</sub>
<a id="migrate.Grants"></a>

### migrate.Grants

```go
func Grants(roles []string) ([]string, error)
```

Grants are the statements that give each runtime role what the stores need of the schema (Options.RuntimeRoles), for a consumer that applies Steps with a tool of its own: ddl.Grants.

<sub>[pgstore/migrate/migrate.go](../../pgstore/migrate/migrate.go)</sub>
<a id="migrate.Run"></a>

### migrate.Run

```go
func Run(ctx context.Context, conn *pgx.Conn, opts Options) error
```

Run brings the store's schema up to the one this version of the package queries, running each migration not yet applied in order, then grants the runtime roles opts names. It refuses a nil conn with limes.ErrInvalidRequest, and a schema of its name owned by another role with ErrSchemaOwner. Run it before the stores serve, as the role that owns the schema, and before any migration of the consumer's that refers to its tables.

It holds a session advisory lock while it migrates, so replicas starting together migrate once. The lock is the one every migration run by github.com/jackc/tern takes; it is reentrant within one session, so a consumer migrating with tern runs Run on the connection its own run holds, never on a second one, which would wait on that run for ever. A consumer with another migration tool runs Run before it, or applies Steps with that tool instead.

Migration 014, which pgstore v0.31.0 brought, now builds its three indexes CONCURRENTLY, outside a transaction, holding no writes, as every later migration that indexes an existing table does, so a Run at startup holds none. Its first form, in v0.31.0 and the releases up to the one that changed it, built them with a plain CREATE INDEX, which held writes to limes.capabilities and limes.revocations for some seconds on a million records; a store that ran that one has the indexes, and tern does not run 014 there again.

Migration 015 adds limes.capabilities.revoked, the flag ListRecords and CountRecords read: a change of the catalog, which rewrites no row and holds the table only for that moment. 016 then marks the records revoked before it, taking only their rows, and 017 builds its indexes CONCURRENTLY.

Migrate before the pgstore that needs a migration serves: a pgstore reads only the schema of its own version (pgstore.CheckSchema says whether it is there). 020, for one, gives limes.revocation\_lineage a column the pgstore of that version reads; an older pgstore reads the function by its columns' names and goes on working beside it, so migrating first is the safe order of a rolling upgrade.

Run needs one connection, not a pool; over a pool:

	err := pool.AcquireFunc(ctx, func(c *pgxpool.Conn) error {
		return migrate.Run(ctx, c.Conn(), migrate.Options{RuntimeRoles: []string{"app"}})
	})

<sub>[pgstore/migrate/migrate.go](../../pgstore/migrate/migrate.go)</sub>
<a id="migrate.Setup"></a>

### migrate.Setup

```go
func Setup() string
```

Setup is the SQL a consumer's tool runs once, before the first Step: ddl.Setup.

<sub>[pgstore/migrate/migrate.go](../../pgstore/migrate/migrate.go)</sub>
<a id="migrate.Options"></a>

### migrate.Options

```go
type Options struct {
	// RuntimeRoles are the roles the stores serve as: roles that own nothing
	// in the schema, which pgstore.CheckSchema checks. Each gets USAGE on the
	// schema, SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE on its tables, SELECT alone
	// on the version table (for CheckSchema), EXECUTE on its functions —
	// which no other role has — USAGE on its sequences, and the same on
	// every table and sequence a later migration creates (ddl.Grants). An
	// empty name, or "public" in any case, is refused (ddl.CheckRuntimeRoles). Granting is idempotent, so each Run grants again.
	// Empty: Run grants nothing, and the roles are the consumer's to grant
	// (Grants).
	RuntimeRoles []string
}
```

Options configures Run.

<sub>[pgstore/migrate/migrate.go](../../pgstore/migrate/migrate.go)</sub>
<a id="migrate.Step"></a>

### migrate.Step

```go
type Step struct {
	// Version is the schema's version once the step has run: tern's
	// numbering, from one without a gap.
	Version int
	// Name is the migration's file name, such as "001_records.sql".
	Name string
	// Migration is the migration's SQL as tern renders and Run runs it.
	// Apply SQL or Statements rather than this.
	Migration string
	// InTransaction says how to run the step: SQL as one transaction of its
	// own; or, when false, Statements a statement at a time outside any
	// transaction, as CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY needs.
	InTransaction bool
}
```

Step is one migration as a consumer's own migration tool applies it, as ddl.Step is, which a program that vendors the SQL imports without tern.
