<a id="ddl"></a><a id="package-ddl"></a>

## Package ddl

`import "github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes/pgstore/migrate/ddl"`

Package ddl is pgstore's schema as data: the migrations, the SQL that creates the version table before them, and the grants after, for a consumer that applies them with a migration tool of its own (docs/adr/0011-migrations-as-data.md). Beyond the standard library it imports only two leaf packages of limes's own (internal/errs and pgstore/internal/pgschema), so a program that vendors the SQL links neither tern nor a driver; pgstore/migrate runs the same migrations itself.

A tool applies Setup once, then each Step not yet applied, in order, then Grants. Each transactional step runs in a transaction of its own: it opens by setting the transaction READ COMMITTED, which PostgreSQL accepts only as a transaction's first statement, and which migration 016 needs, since it reads each level of records by the next statement's snapshot. A non-transactional step runs a statement at a time outside any transaction, as CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY needs (Step.Statements).

<a id="ddl.MigrationsDir"></a>

### ddl.MigrationsDir

```go
const MigrationsDir = "migrations"
```

MigrationsDir is where Files keeps the migrations.

<sub>[pgstore/migrate/ddl/ddl.go](../../pgstore/migrate/ddl/ddl.go)</sub>
<a id="ddl.CheckRuntimeRoles"></a>

### ddl.CheckRuntimeRoles

```go
func CheckRuntimeRoles(roles []string) error
```

CheckRuntimeRoles refuses, with an error matching limes.ErrInvalidConfig, a runtime role that is not one role: an empty name, "public" in any case, which would grant every role, and a name with a NUL, which the identifier quoting drops, granting another role than the one named.

<sub>[pgstore/migrate/ddl/ddl.go](../../pgstore/migrate/ddl/ddl.go)</sub>
<a id="ddl.Files"></a>

### ddl.Files

```go
func Files() fs.FS
```

Files are the migrations as files, under MigrationsDir: for a tool that reads a directory, and for pgstore/migrate's tern.

<sub>[pgstore/migrate/ddl/ddl.go](../../pgstore/migrate/ddl/ddl.go)</sub>
<a id="ddl.Grants"></a>

### ddl.Grants

```go
func Grants(roles []string) ([]string, error)
```

Grants are the statements that give each runtime role what the stores need of the schema: USAGE on it, SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE on its tables, SELECT alone on the version table, EXECUTE on its functions, USAGE on its sequences, which the counters' defaults draw from, and the same on every table and sequence a later step creates. Run them in one transaction after the last step, and again after each later one. It refuses a name that is not one role (CheckRuntimeRoles).

<sub>[pgstore/migrate/ddl/ddl.go](../../pgstore/migrate/ddl/ddl.go)</sub>
<a id="ddl.Setup"></a>

### ddl.Setup

```go
func Setup() string
```

Setup is the SQL a consumer's tool runs once, before the first Step: it creates the schema and the version table at version 0. Run it as the role that owns the schema and applies the steps.

<sub>[pgstore/migrate/ddl/ddl.go](../../pgstore/migrate/ddl/ddl.go)</sub>
<a id="ddl.Version"></a>

### ddl.Version

```go
func Version() int
```

Version is the last migration's: the version a schema is at once every step has run, and the one pgstore.CheckSchema expects. A vendored copy that a newer pgstore outgrew is behind it. A function, not a constant, so that a release adding a migration changes the value, not the API.

<sub>[pgstore/migrate/ddl/ddl.go](../../pgstore/migrate/ddl/ddl.go)</sub>
<a id="ddl.Step"></a>

### ddl.Step

```go
type Step struct {
	// Version is the schema's version once the step has run: tern's
	// numbering, from one without a gap.
	Version int
	// Name is the migration's file name, such as "001_records.sql".
	Name string
	// Migration is the migration's SQL as its file holds it. Apply SQL or
	// Statements rather than this.
	Migration string
	// InTransaction says how to run the step: SQL as one transaction of its
	// own; or, when false, Statements a statement at a time outside any
	// transaction, as CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY needs.
	InTransaction bool
}
```

Step is one migration as a consumer's own migration tool applies it.

<sub>[pgstore/migrate/ddl/ddl.go](../../pgstore/migrate/ddl/ddl.go)</sub>
<a id="ddl.Steps"></a>

#### ddl.Steps

```go
func Steps() ([]Step, error)
```

Steps are the migrations in order, numbered from one without a gap, as tern numbers them: Setup first, then the steps not yet applied, then Grants. The tool keeps its own record of what it applied; the steps keep pgstore's (Step.SQL).

<sub>[pgstore/migrate/ddl/ddl.go](../../pgstore/migrate/ddl/ddl.go)</sub>
<a id="ddl.Step.SQL"></a>

#### ddl.Step.SQL

```go
func (s Step) SQL() string
```

SQL is what a tool applies for a transactional step: the prelude, the migration, then the version record, ending with a statement terminator. For a non-transactional step it is the migration and the record as one text, which a tool that sends one string runs as an implicit transaction; send Statements instead.

<sub>[pgstore/migrate/ddl/ddl.go](../../pgstore/migrate/ddl/ddl.go)</sub>
<a id="ddl.Step.Statements"></a>

#### ddl.Step.Statements

```go
func (s Step) Statements() []string
```

Statements is the step as a tool sends it. A transactional step is SQL alone, run as one transaction. A non-transactional step is each of its statements and then the version record, to send one at a time outside any transaction. Such a migration holds no dollar-quoted body and ends each statement at a line's end, which is what lets it be split here without a parser; a test holds every one to that.
